options.label: A
options.textMd: why customers never know their own losses.

options.label: C
options.textMd: how a default can create a reason to reveal unusual information before choosing precautions.

options.label: D

options.label: E

explanationMd: The example links limited compensation to a disclosure incentive and then to better precaution choices. It demonstrates the information-forcing function, not a universal rule about liability amounts.

distractorRationale.d: The example introduces an alternative function.
distractorRationale.a: The customer is the party with special information.
distractorRationale.b: The argument depends on the cost and value of communication.
distractorRationale.e: The example uses a compensation limit to encourage disclosure.
